How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

  overall security posture. There is no fiscal impact to the City’s General Fund.

   A. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TYLER TECHNOLOGIES FOR
  THE PURCHASE, IMPLEMENTATION, AND SOFTWARE LICENSING AND
  MAINTENANCE OF TYLER’S ENTERPRISE RESOURCE PLANNING (ERP)
  SOFTWARE FOR A ONE-TIME COST OF $417,208 AND ANNUAL
  SUBSCRIPTION OF $125,169

  The City of San Gabriel currently utilizes Tyler Technologies’ Eden system for
  financial management, which has been in place for over 22 years. However,
  Tyler has announced that support for Eden will end in February 2027,
  necessitating the transition to a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system
  to avoid operational disruptions. After a thorough evaluation process, which
  included a comprehensive needs assessment and vendor demonstrations, Tyler
  Technologies' Enterprise ERP system emerged as the best solution to meet the
  City’s financial and human resource management needs. The new system will
  integrate financial management, payroll, human resources, procurement,
  budgeting, and reporting, improving efficiency and eliminating outdated,
  paper-based processes. The total one-time implementation cost is $417,208,
  with an annual subscription fee of $125,169. The implementation will take
  approximately 18 to 24 months, beginning October 1, 2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a subscription-based software agreement with Tyler Technologies for the
  Enterprise ERP system.

MINUTES OF APRIL 1, 2025
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:42 P.M.
  on Tuesday, April 1, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive,
  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Menchaca.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief Steven Wallace;
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias, Finance Director William Kaholokula, Police
  Chief Edward Elizalde, Acting Public Works Director/
  City Engineer Szeka Cheng, Acting Community
  Development Director Samantha Tewasart, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Wu approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

I  A. RECOGNITION OF FIRE DEPARTMENT PROMOTION

  Fire Chief Wallace made the presentation to Fire Captain Takahiro Suzuki and Chief
  City Clerk Clark administered a ceremonial oath of office. Fire Captain Suzuki's
  badge was pinned by his wife Valerie and daughters Satsu and Kanna.

  B. RECOGNITION OF RECREATION COORDINATOR JACKIE VILLALVAZO FOR
  RECEIPIENT OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AWARD OF EXCELLENCE - RISING
  PROFESSIONAL FROM CALIFORNIA PARKS AND RECREATION SOCIETY

  Community Services Director Perez made the presentation.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Ding, to

I  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4C as presented.

  NOES:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of
  March 18, 2025.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved March 6 and 14, 2025, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

I  C. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 25-16 APPROVING A 2024 STATE AND
  LOCAL CYBERSECURITY GRANT PROGRAM (SLCGP) FROM CALIFORNIA
  GOVERNOR'S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF

  1. Authorized the City Manager to sign the Governing Body Form .

  3. Authorized the City Manager to sign the Purchase Order with Darktrace.

I  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TYLER TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE
  PURCHASE, IMPLEMENTATION, AND SOFTWARE LICENSING AND
  MAINTENANCE OF TYLER'S ENTERPRISE RESOURCE PLANNING (ERP)
  SOFTWARE FOR A ONE-TIME COST OF $417,208 AND ANNUAL
  SUBSCRIPTION OF $125,169

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  Apri l 1, 2025
   Clarifying discussion included the timeline for implementation, yearly subscription
  cost, and training details.

  There was no public comment.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Chan,
  to authorize the City Manager to execute a subscription-based software agreement
  with Tyler Technologies for the Enterprise ERP system.

I  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  a) Selection of Mayor

  Chief City Clerk Clark declared the offices of Mayor and Vice Mayor vacant and
  opened the floor for nominations.

  Council Member Ding nominated Council Member Menchaca. Hearing no other
  nominations, Chief City Clerk Clark declared Council Member Menchaca
  selected as Mayor by acclamation.

  b) Selection of Vice Mayor

I  Mayor Menchaca opened the floor for nominations for Vice Mayor. Council
  Member Herrera Avila nominated Council Member Chan. Hearing no other
  nominations, Mayor Menchaca declared Council Member Chan selected as Vice
  Mayor by acclamation.

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT - None.

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Chan reported on his attendance at a fundraiser for retired San Gabriel

  thanked outgoing Mayor Wu and City staff, Arcadia Chamber of Commerce
  networking lunch meeting, and Pasadena Chamber of Commerce networking
  fundraiser for victims of the Eaton Fire.

  Council Member Herrera Avila congratulated incoming Mayor Menchaca and Vice
  Mayor Chan and thanked outgoing Mayor Wu for leading the City.

I  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at a San Gabriel Valley Legislative
  Caucus Meet and Greet, Chinese Women's Business Association seminar, San Gabriel
  State of the City address, Los Angeles County "Government Connections Networking
  Seminar, and iTaiwan Foods Temple City sto fe grand opening; and congratulated
  incoming Mayor Menchaca and Vice Mayor Chan and outgoing Mayor Wu.

  Council Member Wu congratulated incoming Mayor Menchaca and Vice Mayor Chan
  and thanked his colleagues for all they accomplished together during his term as
  mayor. Regarding the State of the City event, he thanked City Manager Lazzaretto,

   Public Information Officer Iliana Flores, Management Assistant Jessica Zhao, City
  department heads, and Police and Fire Departments for the honor guard. In closing,
  he reported on his attendance at a meeting hosted by the Office of Los Angeles
  County Supervisor Hilda Solis regarding the 2028 Olympics.

  Mayor Menchaca reported on her attendance at a fundraiser for retired Police
  Detective Malette, a Chinese Women's Business Association workshop, Ramadan
  event at the San Gabriel Mosque, and the State of the City address and commended
  outgoing Mayor Wu; and commented on the City being ahead of the curve in having

I  drone shows instead of fireworks for the Independence Day event.
